title: Edie and the Polite Ploys
markdown:
Dawn peeked through the library windows, a brilliant burst of golden light. Outside, birds chirped their wake-up songs. Sunlight splashed across the polished floors, making them gleam like a spilled pot of paint. Edie the duck stretched her neck, beak clicking with bubbling excitement. Today was THE day. The Library Marble Championship was about to start.

Edie was a champion. A proper, dazzling, marble-bouncing champion. Her speedy flick of the wrist was legendary, her beak-tucked-in focus unbreakable. Nobody could beat her. Or so she thought. Whispers had been buzzing, like busy bees, about a new challenger. Headmistress Plum.

“Ready, Cas?” Edie quacked, webbed feet tapping a frantic rhythm. Cas the cat, a sleek tabby with amazing stripes, blinked slowly from his prime sunbeam perch. He stretched, a long lazy movement that ended with a soft Mrow, a gentle rumble. Cas mostly enjoyed the quiet snoozy naps that followed Edie’s triumphs.

Edie hopped to her special marble bag. The glittering galaxy swirl, colours spinning like a tiny universe. The bouncy blue marble named Bob, always up for a good game. Her lucky rainbow shooter, bursting with every colour imaginable. She practiced her signature flick. Pock! Perfect. Pock! Pock! Faster. The familiar thrill zinged through her. She leaped and spun her marbles with quick taps.

The library was already buzzing. Excited faces packed the reading nooks. All eyes on the grand marble arena, a circle of polished wood near the tall shelves of biography books. And there, at the opponents’ table, sat Headmistress Plum. Kind smile. Neat buttoned cardigan that looked impossibly tidy.

“Good morning, Edie!” Voice like a cascade of tinkling bells. “Such a delight to be participating. I do hope you’ve had a splendid breakfast. Perhaps some delicious plump berries?”

Edie blinked. A splendid breakfast? What did that have to do with marbles? “Um, yes, Headmistress! Lots of crunchy worms and a big juicy slug!” Mind already racing with her first move.

The game began. Edie flicked her galaxy swirl. Pock! It zoomed, knocking three other marbles far away. Cas, from his sunbeam, let out a tiny silent yawn, a mere opening of his pink mouth. Ready for nap number one.

Headmistress Plum’s turn. She carefully picked up a plain speckled grey marble. “Would you be so kind as to hold this for me, dear?” A nearby child, bright-eyed, clutching a teddy, obliged. “Thank you so much!” Smile as warm as the morning sun.

Edie’s beak clicked impatiently. This was taking ages.

Plum lined up her shot. “Oh, pardon me,” she murmured, as her marble gently nudged another, a tiny barely-there tap. “I do apologize for that tiny problem. I hope I haven’t caused you any trouble.”

Edie’s feathers prickled. She needed to flick Bob right into the centre. Flick! But just as her webbed foot prepared the powerful push, Plum piped up again, voice light as a dandelion puff.

“Edie, dear, your quills are looking particularly glossy today. Have you been using a special sort of sparkly pond water? They catch the light so beautifully.”

Edie froze mid-flick. Glossy quills? She glanced down. They did look rather shiny, reflecting the bright sunlight. She’d never really noticed.

“Oh, thank you!” Completely forgetting her shot. As she looked down, a puff of air escaped her surprised gasp. Plum’s marble, nudged by that gentle puff, rolled ever so slightly. It nudged Edie’s shooter. It rolled, ever so slowly, ever so deliberately, into a tricky, almost impossible-to-reach corner.

“Oh, my goodness!” Mock surprise. “Did I? I am terribly sorry! I hope that wasn’t too troublesome. Please do tell me if I have caused any bother at all!”

Troublesome? Edie’s beak clacked, rapid-fire. Utterly bizarre. Plum’s politeness was a fluffy white cloud, soft and completely overwhelming. It floated between Edie and her winning shots. Every time Edie prepared to flick, Plum offered a compliment, asked a gentle innocent question, or apologized for something entirely accidental.

“Your focus is truly admirable, Edie. Though, if I may be so bold, the light is rather bright on this particular side. Perhaps if you just shifted a tiny bit… Oh, but please don’t trouble yourself on my account!”

Edie found herself apologizing for her own breathing. Too busy saying Thank you and It’s quite alright and No bother at all to actually play marbles. She even apologized for the sound of her own quacking.

Finally, with a gentle almost apologetic tap, Plum’s marble nudged Edie’s very last marble. It wobbled, then, with a tiny clatter, rolled out of the arena.

“Oh, dear.” Eyes twinkling like mischievous stars. “It appears I have won. My sincerest apologies, Edie. I had no intention of besting such a magnificent player. You are truly a wonder.”

The crowd gasped. Edie stared. She’d lost. Not to a powerful flick, not to a clever strategy, but to an unstoppable avalanche of thank-yous and pardon-mes. The most ridiculous, unexpected defeat ever.

Cas stretched and ambled over, tail giving a gentle swish. He nudged Edie’s head with his soft nose. Mrow? Whiskers twitching sympathetically.

Edie looked at Plum, who was now happily, and apologetically, rearranging the marbles. A little giggle, then a bigger chuckle, bubbled up. The funniest thing that had ever happened. “Headmistress, you are the most delightfully distracting marble player I have ever, ever met.”

Plum beamed, smile reaching all the way to her ears. “Why, thank you, Edie! That is most kind. I do try my best.”

Edie picked up her marbles, heart still thrumming with a strange wonderful giggly energy. She hadn’t won the sparkling trophy this year. She had discovered something far more interesting and hilarious: a champion could be undone by please and thank you, and still leave the library bouncing. With a bouncy excited quack she raced out the door, webbed feet pattering, ready for whatever wonderfully peculiar adventure the bright bustling day had in store.
characters: Edie (a duck), Cas (a cat), Plum (a headmistress)
author: StoryGen Community
